links.comparator_used: Standard direct prompting (no chain-of-thought) on the same model, for both MedGo and DeepSeek
links.effect: MedGo 4.25±0.16 to 4.58±0.09 with CoT (Holm-adjusted p=0.024); DeepSeek 3.98±0.20 to 4.41±0.11 with CoT (Holm-adjusted p<0.001); score dispersion reduced
links.quote: CoT improved both models (Holm-adjusted p<0.001 for DeepSeek; p=0.024 for MedGo) and reduced score dispersion.

links.comparator_used: General-purpose model DeepSeek V3.5 (both under direct prompting and under CoT prompting)
links.outcome: Physician-rated comprehensive antibiotic regimen score, plus individualized adjustment and dosing precision sub-scores
links.effect: Base mode: MedGo 4.25±0.16 vs DeepSeek 3.98±0.20 (Holm-adjusted p=0.040). With CoT: MedGo 4.58±0.09 vs DeepSeek 4.41±0.11, better on individualized adjustment (adjusted p<0.001) and dosing precision (adjusted p=0.005)
links.tradeoff: Deficiencies persisted in antimicrobial stewardship ecological awareness, and real physicians still scored higher (4.76±0.04)
links.quote: In base mode, MedGo significantly outperformed DeepSeek (Holm-adjusted p=0.040).

links.comparator_used: Senior clinician expert ratings of the regimens
links.outcome: Agreement between ChatGPT 5.2 automated scores and expert clinician scores
links.effect: Overall Kendall τ=0.153 (p=0.003); subgroup τ=0.06-0.20, all p>0.05
links.tradeoff: Automated evaluation reliability was poor, so it could not replace senior clinical expertise
links.quote: ChatGPT–expert correlation was negligible (overall Kendall τ=0.153, p=0.003; subgroup τ=0.06–0.20, all p>0.05).
